title: The Heavenly Spheres to Thee, O God
description: The Heavenly Spheres to Thee, O God in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 399, “The Hymn of the Seasons”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: The heav-enly spheres to Thee, O God, At-tune their eve-ning hymn; All wise, all ho-ly, Thou art praised In song of ser-a-phim. Un-num-bered sys-tems, suns, and worlds, U-nite to wor-ship Thee, While Thy ma-jes-tic great-ness fills Space, time, e-ter-ni-ty.

lines: The heavenly spheres to Thee, O God,
Beams with Thy light and love;
Whose flowers so sweetly bloom below,
Her song of gratitude is sung
Her Summer offers at Thy shrine
Her Autumn brings its golden fruits,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
